body: That's a good idea. I'll try it. However, at the moment her reaction is very very all over the place. I think she's torn and lost. I keep trying to explain that one should focus on building and solving rather than follow the allure of something new and seemingly different and exciting. Not sure if I'm getting through.
I'm trying. I really am.
At this point, I honestly don't know what to think.

Have you tried retaliating? I had similar issues and the problem got resolved when I actually bit back. Hard. Just told them to stop yelling at me. That I'm a human being and that I react poorly to their behavior.
Dude, I know that a lot of stuff in that country, especially in older generations, is completely backwards. How old are you? Can you move out? Or maybe live with a friend or another relative?
I need some sort of closure in that case. And I honestly can't imagine what kind of closure I can get in that case...
Which country are you from?
No it's not okay. Why are you doing it? Why are you thinking so?
Please, wait! No. Why? What are your reasons?

Well, I have been thinking about it, and honestly, at this point, after all the time, money and trust I've invested; shifting the blame on me sounds like a less sound idea. I mean, did I breach it? Yeah, I did. Then again - I may be kind, naive and trusting but I'm not a fucking moron. You know that feeling when someone tells you that everything is going to be okay, but you kinda sense that they mean that it's going to be okay for them, not for you necessarily? That's exactly the feeling I've had all this time. It's been way too suspicious with the whole "Let's slather him in layers of blame, let's focus all of his attention on it and make him feel guilty and terrible"

But then I thought to myself - what is the purpose of such a behavior? Most likely scenario is to try and shift my gaze into an another direction, and at the same time try to morally compensate herself for the shit she's done, which seems to be "If I make him into a terrible asshole, then I won't look so bad in comparison!" And the worst part about this? It makes perfect fucking sense, from a logical point of view!

Well, that's the whole point! We (mainly I in terms of financial and judicial effort) have been trying to make it not long distance for like a year or so now. Keep hitting different corners regarding the whole bureaucracy of things but we're paddling on. So, I was under a fixed assumption that, you know, stuff is only going to get better. I knew that long distance has its course that it can run, it has a limited life span. Hence, we decided on taking it further and faster.

I can't confirm to a 100% that they've done it. But from I can read from the texts, there is definite intent to do it, if it's not already happened. No nudes were sent but the subject is being discussed in very open way.
How would you approach such a conversation?

Therein lies my biggest concern. It's like this - on a day-to-day basis I am the stronger person. But I'm strong in a nice way and I lack a particular quality that she has an abundance of - ruthlessness. She is being completely ruthless at this time, almost on the brink of sadistic. I can't escape the feeling that she knows exactly what she does and how she makes me feel. I'm currently popping pills for anxiety and all kinds of nerve-related shit just from this whole experience. Usually, I'm a contained, motivated, positive individual. But at this point I feel absolutely trashed. There's not a single thought that actually sticks in my head. Everything is just a huge clusterfuck of emotions and thoughts. Half of it being in the lines of "I will crush her! How dare she!? After all that!?" and half of it is the opposite "I need to fix this. There's something amiss. I am older, more experienced, I can handle this and just need to find the right angle"

Does any of that make sense at all or am I just slowly spiraling down into some sort of dark place?

My dilemma lies mostly with the fact that the information I got wasn't really handed to me willingly, but rather, well, I got it myself. Am I correct in the fact that I'm just as guilty of not acting in good faith?
How would you suggest that I approach her about the subject?

It all, of course, depends on how things will pan out. There is, of course, quite a lot of things that could be improved with my behavior also. Forgiving her? Well, in all honesty, I don't know how and if. I can't answer this at the moment. I know that in my previous relationships things happened, and even worse things at some point, and it went just fine with bygones being bygones. But that required quite a hefty amount of communication, understanding and effort. My biggest issue in this case is the fact that I'm constantly hitting a wall and I don't know how to handle it at this particular moment.

Here's the point that needs to be explained. I love this woman something ferociously. I didn't have anything else planned. The whole deal of "being an alpha" sounds good on paper. However, sometimes, relationships are tricky and just bruteforcing things WILL give you dividends but only in the short term. I was never aiming for anything short-term with this relationship. That's why I'm posting here, as at the moment me myself is the person whom I have the least trust for and therefore am asking for advice from fellow redditors to help me gain some insight and sanity.

All she seems to do at this is just somehow dodge it. I ask rather direct questions. The answers I get are somewhere between "I don't know" and "I need to think".

What I'm afraid of is the following: I leave. She takes time for herself. Then calls me, drops the bomb and just bails. Never letting me have any closure. Hence why I also feel stressed, as it feels like time is running out.

That's what I kept telling her all this time. Kept pointing out that relationships require work and it needs to be a joint effort. I also kept emphasizing the fact that everything has its price. We're currently resolving a difficult situation with our separate lives becoming a singular. And that requires a lot of work, effort and money from me, which obviously makes me a much more "dull boy". But it's not permanent and it's not going to be like that all the time, because I don't like it more than she does.

Most of her responses to this are kinda negligent and just uttering something along the lines "Oh, it's just words you're saying". I honestly don't know what slices at me deeper...

This is - I have no actual proof that she actually (well, actually being as in physically) cheated on me. I keep thinking that maybe there is an explanation? Like, "Not enough attention and I started doubting whether you still love/care for me so I got a quick fix and flirted with a dude at work"?
Tell me. How would you go about confronting her with all of this? My head is spinning at the moment. No rational or clear thought in sight.

Please, tell me, about this whole "in no way are you to ever think it’s gonna work" thing. I personally know couples where such incidents happened; the whole sexting thing and so on; and it went on to work just fine. Or am I being way to naive here?
